On Wed, Jun 20, 2012 at 1:20 PM, dtenenba <dand...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hello,
> I changed some of the Rhipe examples from the github wiki to do what I want
> to do, and it works, but it looks like the mapper only runs once, instead of
> once per piece of input data which is what I would like.
> It's also possible that the way I have put my code together is not well
> thought-out.
>
> What I did was change the word count generator example to generate some
> strings of input data to process.
> Then I created another mapreduce job, based on the word count example (with
> no reduce function, because I don't need one) which takes a piece of that
> input data and does some processing to it and then writes out some output.
> It works but it seems, judging from the output, that the mapper only ran
> once.
>
> I realize that maybe I should change this to a single mapreduce job, where
> the mapper runs just once and creates all the input data, and the reducer
> processes it. I have tried that and run into problems. So I thought it would
> be best to post about what actually works and ask how I can get it to work
> the proper number of times, and then maybe incrementally get to a better way
> of doing it.
>
> So first, off, some dependencies are required in order to do this, if you
> want to try it yourself:
> You must be running R-2.15.
> Do the following:
> source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
> useDevel()
> biocLite(c("snpStats", "VariantAnnotation",
> "TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene"))
>
> Outside of R, do this (because this package is not part of Bioconductor):
> svn co --username readonly --password
> readonly https://hedgehog.fhcrc.org/bioconductor/trunk/madman/Rpacks/BiocCloud/
> R CMD INSTALL BiocCloud
> (if the above step complains about missing dependencies, install them)
>
> Now, here is what actually works:
>
> Step 1, generate input data:
>
> library(Rhipe)
> rhinit()
>
> makeDataSet <- function(N, dest, local=TRUE)
> {
>     map <- as.expression(bquote({
>         N <- .(N)
>         urls <- getBucketUrls()
>         txdb <- TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene
>         cds <- cds(txdb)
>         cds <- reduce(keepSeqlevels(cds, paste("chr", 1:22, sep="")))
>         values(cds)[["Url"]] <- urls[as.character(seqnames(cds))]
>         map <- setNames(sub("chr", "", seqlevels(cds)), seqlevels(cds))
>         cds <- renameSeqlevels(cds, map)
>         ## Return a regular R list
>         tasks <- Map(function(...) list(...),
>             seqnames=as.character(seqnames(cds)), start=start(cds),
>             end=end(cds), url=values(cds)$Url,
> MoreArgs=list(genome=unique(genome(cds))))
>
>         if (N > length(tasks)) N <- length(tasks)
>
>
>         for (i in 1:N)
>         {
>             row = tasks[[i]]
>             line <- sprintf("%s %s %s %s %s", row$seqnames, row$start,
> row$end,
>                 row$url, row$genome)
>             rhcollect(NULL, line)
>         }
>
>     }, list()))
>     mapred <- list()
>     if (local) mapred$mapred.job.tracker <- 'local'
>     mapred$mapred.field.separator=" "
>     mapred$mapred.textoutputformat.usekey=FALSE
>     mapred$mapred.map.tasks=1
>     z <- rhmr(map=map, N=N,ofolder=dest,inout=c("lapp","text"),
>          mapred=mapred,
>          setup=list(map=expression({
>              suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(BiocCloud))
>              suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(VariantAnnotation))
>
>  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene))
>              suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(snpStats))
>          })))
>     rhex(z)
>
> }
>
> N <- 10
> filename <- sprintf("/tmp/%s",paste(sample(letters,6),collapse=""))
> makeDataSet(N,filename)
> message(sprintf("Input created in %s",filename))
>
> That works and creates a file in the 'filename' directory that looks like
> this:

> hg19

> hg19

> hg19

>

> really create 200,000 mappers or just intelligently send the data in

> 200,000 mappers but I do want each line of input to be processed in
> isolation. )

I haven't got around to it, but i will, this week. sorry for the delay.
as for this, if you have N files, you;llhave >=N splits.
But as you pointed out you don't want 200K files. Correct.

But if you have a file with 200K lines, it's most likely going to be
<= 1 block size (e.g. 128MB).
Each block is a map. So if you have 1 block, you'll have 1 map.

Now, depending on how long the computation is you can have M mappers
among which you schedule N lines
e.g. like N/M lines of text. Which means you'd have to have not 200K
files, but maybe 1000 files.
(which in my opinion is too large).

The problem is simplified if you can compute a line given a number from 1..N
Then use rhmr(map,N=N (here N=200K),
mapred=list(mapred.map.tasks=1000)) and in the map compute the line
corresponding to i.

(setting mapped.map.tasks=N, is not such a good idea if the time taken
to compute for N is smaller than the time taken
to start the map task, this is true for many  task distributers).

On another note, is Hbase a viable option? I might have an option to
(at least) read from Hbase. then you're do as above
and for key=i (i-1...N), read the i'th row from an Hbase table.

Cheers
Saptarshi

New stuff in rhread, rhwatch, rhmr. Also this new way of invoking
commands is pretty useful.

m <- rhmap({
  rhcollect(sample(1:5,1), sample(1:5,1))
})

           {
             rhcollect(reduce.key, list(all=adata,mean=mean(adata[,1])))
           })
z <- rhwatch(rhmr(map=m, reduce=r,combine=FALSE, N=10))

The above outputs random number from 1;5, associated with a key from 1:5
The reducer assembles these  into data frame and computes the mean.

Other reducers are rhoptions()$templates${scalar summer, range, colsummer}

rhwatch has debug facilities
rhwatch can also take user code to monitor the execution etc.
